tennis._note: Owner, 2026-10-12: 'For tennis, only give me results of top 5. Make sure we follow any tennis the top 5 are in.' The top N is read live from the tour rankings, so it follows whoever is actually in the top 5 - it is not a fixed list of names. Only matches involving a top-N player are reported, and they are reported for whichever tournament those players are in, so a top-5 player is never missed.

settings._note: news_max_age_days is widened automatically for the weekly run. total_budget_seconds stops the whole research step if the network is slow, so the email always goes out on time.

local._note: What to look for near you. Set a category's enabled=false to mute it - the same switch the sport list uses. `priority` is the owner's own preference order (lower first) and is the order the digest renders; absent means configured order. `annual` marks a category whose events come round once a year: those are judged against annual_months_ahead, everything else against months_ahead. `two_person` adds the couples / for-two search the owner asked for ('nice massage sale i can take Chloe and i, same with buffets'); it is additive and never suppresses the solo results. An empty category says so rather than inventing something.
local.source: Owner, 2026-11-05: 'I am in Wilgeheuwel.' and 'you should be reading pages for me and giving me best names of places to go for buffets and if they are limited etc. Also nice date night specials around me.'
local._read_pages_note: The owner rejected headline-only output ('lazy to just give news headlines'). Each item now carries the venue/place name where one can be read from the page, plus any limits or conditions found on it. Where nothing can be read the item says so rather than dressing a headline up as a recommendation.

price_watch._note: Exactly the items the owner listed, with the reference page he gave for each. `ref_url` is the page he considers the product: it is fetched directly for his own cheapest-known price, and Takealot's search supplies competing offers. `top_n` is how many cheapest to show. `include_used` asks the sources for second-hand listings too. A saving is only ever the difference between two REAL listed prices, never an estimate.
price_watch.source: Owner, 2026-11-05: 'Show me top 3 cheapest you can find of exact things i need as well as highlight if any below market price. Look for new and 2nd hand please. Black friday specials would be apprecaited.'
price_watch._strict_note: `must_not_match` and `ddr` exist because a loose match reported a cheaper DIFFERENT product as 'below market': a DDR4 3600 kit showed as 59% under a DDR5 5600 watch, and three other motherboard brands matched 'b850m'. A wrong-product price is worse than no price.

_removed_series_note: Series the owner does not want. Matched case-insensitively against an event's `series`. This exists because the three he removed all sit under Motorsport, which he still wants for MotoGP and F1 - a sport-level mute would have taken those with it.
